Important Notice
The Board of Directors, Directors and the senior management of the Bank undertake that the information in this report is true,
accurate and complete and contains no false records, misleading statements or material omissions, and they assume individual
and joint legal liabilities for such information.


The 2025 annual report, highlights and results announcement were reviewed and approved at the meeting of the Board of
Directors of the Bank held on March 27, 2026. The number of Directors who should attend the meeting is 17, among which 17
Directors attended the meeting in person. The attendance was in compliance with the requirements of the Company Law of
the People’s Republic of China and the Articles of Association.


In accordance with the Company Law of the People’s Republic of China, the Administrative Measures for Provisioning
of Financial Enterprises, the Articles of Association and relevant requirements, the final cash dividends for 2025 totaling
approximately RMB11,445 million (before tax) will be distributed to all ordinary shareholders whose names appeared on the
share register on the record date at RMB0.953 (before tax) per ten ordinary shares. Together with the interim cash dividends
for 2025 already paid, the total cash dividends for the whole year of 2025 will be approximately RMB26,217 million (before
tax) at RMB2.183 (before tax) per ten ordinary shares. The Bank did not convert its capital reserve to share capital in 2025. The
aforesaid profit distribution scheme is subject to review and approval at the 2025 Annual General Meeting. For details of the
Bank’s profit during the reporting period, please refer to “Discussion and Analysis – Analysis of Financial Statements”.


During the reporting period, there was no appropriation of the Bank’s funds by its controlling shareholder or other related
parties for non-operating purposes and no case in which the Bank provided material guarantees in violation of the prescribed
decision-making procedures.


The financial report of the Bank for the year 2025, prepared in accordance with PRC GAAP and IFRSs, has been audited by
KPMG Huazhen LLP and KPMG in accordance with domestic and international auditing standards respectively with unqualified
auditor’s reports issued.

Company Profile




The postal savings business in China can be traced back to its start in 1919 with a history of over one hundred years. In March
2007, based on the reform of the previous postal savings management system, Postal Savings Bank of China Limited was
officially established. The Bank was transformed into a joint stock limited liability company in January 2012. It went public and
was listed on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange in September 2016, and was listed on the SSE in December 2019.

The Bank is a leading large-scale retail bank in China and remains committed to its positioning of serving Sannong customers,
urban and rural residents, and SMEs. Relying on its unique model and resource endowment featuring directly-operated
outlets and agency outlets, it keeps improving its financial service system where online and offline services interconnect for
joint development, and is committed to providing comprehensive financial services to the most promising customers during
China’s economic transformation. As at the end of the reporting period, the Bank had approximately 40,000 outlets and served
over 680 million personal customers, continuing to maintain excellent asset quality and an increasingly prominent market
presence.

The Bank gains a profound understanding of the political and people-oriented nature of financial work, thoroughly implements
national strategies, and continues to enhance the quality and efficiency in serving the real economy. It adheres to the
customer-centric philosophy and attaches great importance to creating value for customers. The Bank has pressed ahead with
the “five priorities” of technology finance, green finance, inclusive finance, pension finance and digital finance and accelerated
the upgrading toward distinctive, light, integrated, ecosystem-based, refined, and digital and intelligent development. It strives
to build a first-tier large retail bank that is more inclusive, balanced, stable, intelligent and dynamic, and create a new chapter
of high-quality development.

Colourful PSBC                                                                    Establishing Featured Financial Brand with
                                                                                  Caring Services to Celebrate Ethnic Diversity

Ethnic minority culture is an integral part of Chinese culture. With featured sub-branches as a platform, the Bank fulfills
its mission of “delivering accessible financial services in both urban and rural areas”. In areas densely populated by ethnic
minorities such as the Korean, Shui, and Naxi ethnic groups, the Bank has established a number of ethnic culture featured
sub-branches, continuously enhanced the accessibility of financial services, and supported the inheritance and development
of ethnic minority culture.

            Sandu County Sub-Branch, Qiannan Buyei and
            Miao Autonomous Prefecture, Guizhou
            Shui Culture Featured Sub-Branch
         The Sandu County Sub-Branch is located in China’s only Shui Autonomous
         County, where the Shui ethnic group accounts for 67% of the population.
         Building on the characteristics of the local customer base, the sub-branch                                                                                   South China Sea islands




         integrated ethnic culture into its financial services to create a Shui culture
         featured sub-branch. By establishing bilingual service counters in Shui and
         Chinese languages and forming Shui-language service teams to reach villages,
         the sub-branch enhanced communication convenience and improved the
         accessibility of financial services for Shui customers.
         The sub-branch innovatively launched products such as “Xinjie Loan” and
         “Specialty Agricultural Product Cultivation and Breeding Loan” to precisely
         support specialty fields including the Shui people’s horsetail embroidery
         intangible cultural heritage industry and ecological agriculture. These efforts
         have not only injected financial vitality into the inheritance and preservation
         of ethnic culture but also demonstrated the Bank’s commitment to revitalizing
         ethnic minority regions through finance, achieving mutually reinforcing
         development between financial services and ethnic development. During the
         reporting period, the sub-branch served over 2,000 Shui-language-speaking
         customers, conducted eight bilingual financial education activities, and issued
         more than RMB30 million in loans to specialty industries.

    Zhuoshui Town Sub-Branch, Qianjiang District, Chongqing
    Tujia Culture Featured Sub-Branch

Zhuoshui Ancient Town, located in the Wuling Mountain area of southeastern Chongqing,
is a Tujia ethnic community with specialty agriculture and ethnic cultural tourism as core
industries. PSBC Chongqing Branch fully utilized the region’s ethnic cultural characteristics
to upgrade the Zhuoshui Town Sub-Branch located beside traditional stilted houses in
Qianjiang District into a Tujia culture featured sub-branch.
The sub-branch incorporated Tujia “Xilankapu” textile elements into its outlet design
and provided smart services in the functional areas of outlets through virtual reality (VR)
business halls, deeply integrating ethnic culture with modern financial services. It served
not only as a financial service window but also as a carrier of cultural heritage and an
engine for rural revitalization. As at the end of the reporting period, PSBC Chongqing
Branch extended full-village credit to the nine administrative villages in Zhuoshui Town,
disbursed approximately RMB400 million in franchise rights loans for tourist attractions,
and provided acquiring and digital RMB collection services for 400 merchants in Zhuoshui
Ancient Town, strongly supporting the development of local specialty ethnic industries.

Analysis of Financial Statements
During the reporting period, the Bank adhered to the principle of seeking progress while maintaining stability and promoting
stability through progress. It actively advanced strategic upgrades, deepened reform and innovation, and strengthened
internal growth drivers, thereby maintaining a healthy and steady development momentum.


Firstly, the Bank achieved steady growth in scale with a more balanced structure. It focused on serving the real economy
and continuously optimized its asset and liability allocation. As at the end of the reporting period, its total assets reached
RMB18.68 trillion, an increase of 9.35% from the prior year-end, of which total loans to customers amounted to RMB9.65 trillion,
an increase of 8.25% from the prior year-end. Total liabilities reached RMB17.52 trillion, an increase of 9.13% from the prior
year-end, of which customer deposits stood at RMB16.54 trillion, an increase of 8.20% from the prior year-end.


Secondly, the Bank maintained stable profitability with more diversified sources of income. It accelerated business
transformation and actively expanded the sources of income. During the reporting period, the Bank achieved operating
income of RMB355,866 million, an increase of 1.93% compared with the prior year. Specifically, net interest income was
RMB281,620 million, a decrease of 1.57% compared with the prior year, yet the decline continued to narrow; net fee and
commission income totaled RMB29,365 million, an increase of 16.15% compared with the prior year; and net other non-interest
income reached RMB44,881 million, an increase of 18.96% compared with the prior year. Net profit amounted to RMB87,623
million, an increase of 1.05% compared with the prior year.


Thirdly, the Bank continuously recorded stable asset quality indicators, and strictly upheld the bottom line for asset quality
control. The Bank continuously improved the risk management framework that covers “all aspects, whole process, all time and
all areas”, and strengthened risk control and mitigation efforts. As at the end of the reporting period, its non-performing loan
ratio was 0.95%, and allowance to NPLs ratio was 227.94%.

Analysis of Financial Statements
Interest Income
During the reporting period, the Bank realized interest income of RMB480,903 million, a decrease of RMB27,340 million, or
5.38% compared with the prior year, primarily due to the decline in the average yield on interest-earning assets caused by the
ongoing impact of LPR cuts and the downward adjustment of existing mortgage rates. In response to the downward pressure
on interest rates, the Bank adhered to risk-adjusted return on capital (RAROC) as a yardstick, and dynamically optimized its
asset allocation. It implemented a balanced credit supply strategy and a flexible non-credit allocation strategy, facilitating the
steady growth in the scale of interest-earning assets.


Interest Income from Loans to Customers
During the reporting period, interest income from loans to customers amounted to RMB299,527 million, a decrease of
RMB25,194 million, or 7.76% compared with the prior year, primarily due to the decrease in interest income from loans to
personal customers.


Among them, interest income from personal loans amounted to RMB168,408 million, a decrease of RMB28,472 million,
or 14.46% compared with the prior year, primarily due to the decrease in the average yield on personal loans. Seizing
opportunities arising from favorable policies, the Bank created innovative financial products and services, and gave more credit
support to areas such as residential consumption and rural revitalization, contributing to the steady growth in the average
balance of personal consumer loans and micro loans.


Interest income from corporate loans amounted to RMB125,801 million, an increase of RMB3,754 million, or 3.08% compared
with the prior year. It was primarily because the Bank continued to deepen institutional and mechanism reforms, and
comprehensively enhanced its integrated service capabilities for corporate customers. Furthermore, it followed national
strategic orientations and intensified credit supply for key industries, policy-backed businesses and strategic regions, achieving
rapid growth in the average balance of corporate loans.

Interest Income from Investments
During the reporting period, the Bank’s interest income from investments amounted to RMB139,718 million, a decrease of
RMB2,019 million, or 1.42% compared with the prior year, primarily due to the decline in the average yield. The Bank adhered
to the research-driven investment approach, reasonably arranged the pace and maturity of investments, increased allocation to
government bonds with high RAROC, and achieved rapid growth in the average balance of investments, effectively offsetting
the impact of interest rate decline.


Interest Income from Deposits with Central Bank
During the reporting period, the Bank’s interest income from deposits with central bank amounted to RMB20,069 million, a
decrease of RMB183 million, or 0.90% compared with the prior year.


Interest Income from Deposits and Placements with Banks and Other Financial Institutions
During the reporting period, the Bank’s interest income from deposits and placements with banks and other financial
institutions amounted to RMB21,589 million, an increase of RMB56 million, or 0.26% compared with the prior year, primarily
because the Bank increased the scale of its bonds held under resale agreements and deposits with banks and other financial
institutions.


Interest Expense
The Bank continuously strengthened proactive and forward-looking liability management to promote the optimization
of liability structure and steady decline in liability costs. During the reporting period, the interest expense amounted to
RMB199,283 million, a decrease of RMB22,837 million, or 10.28% compared with the prior year.


Interest Expense on Customer Deposits
During the reporting period, interest expense on customer deposits amounted to RMB183,582 million, a decrease of RMB26,635
million, or 12.67% compared with the prior year, primarily because the Bank adhered to the coordinated development
between deposit volume and price, and actively expanded the scale of deposits absorbed from directly-operated outlets, while
benefiting from a decline in the average interest payment rate of customer deposits driven by the downward adjustment of
deposit interest rates. Specifically, the average interest payment rate of personal and corporate deposits decreased by 29 and
21 basis points, respectively.

Net Fee and Commission Income
During the reporting period, the Bank accelerated the capacity building of its intermediary business. While consolidating
its traditional advantages in the retail banking business, the Bank actively developed the businesses of corporate banking
segment and strengthened synergy within the treasury business segment, establishing a diversified and balanced intermediary
income structure. As a result, net fee and commission income amounted to RMB29,365 million, an increase of RMB4,083
million, or 16.15% compared with the prior year.


Fee and commission income amounted to RMB43,424 million, an increase of RMB2,671 million or 6.55% compared with the
prior year. Specifically, wealth management fee income amounted to RMB5,373 million, a year-on-year increase of RMB1,422
million or 35.99%, primarily due to the growth in the sales of wealth management products as the Bank actively seized market
opportunities and enhanced the supply of diversified wealth management products to meet customers’ needs for diversified
asset allocation. Investment banking fee income amounted to RMB4,596 million, a year-on-year increase of RMB1,278 million
or 38.52%. It was mainly because the Bank continuously enhanced the synergy between “commercial banking plus investment
banking” businesses, accelerated the building of a financial service framework integrating investment banking and commercial
banking businesses, and achieved a rapid growth in the income from syndicated loans and financial advisory business. Custody
business fee income amounted to RMB1,423 million, a year-on-year increase of RMB168 million or 13.39%, primarily driven by
the growth in the scale of custody business as the Bank deepened the coordinated development mechanism for the custody
business and optimized the product mix. Other business fee income amounted to RMB3,170 million, a year-on-year increase
of RMB710 million or 28.86%. It was mainly because the Bank provided customers with full-chain, all-scenario, and digital
and intelligent integrated financial services with a focus on the financial needs of upstream and downstream enterprises,
and realized rapid growth in the fee income from supply chain finance, notes, letters of guarantee, letters of credit and other
businesses.


Fee and commission expense amounted to RMB14,059 million, a decrease of RMB1,412 million, or 9.13% compared with the
prior year.

Net Other Non-Interest Income
During the reporting period, the Bank enhanced market analysis and deepened diversified trading strategies. The Bank’s net
other non-interest income amounted to RMB44,881 million, an increase of RMB7,153 million, or 18.96% compared with the
prior year.


Specifically, net trading gains and net gains on investment securities totaled RMB25,335 million, a decrease of RMB8,409
million, or 24.92% compared with the prior year. It was mainly due to the decrease in valuation gains on products such as
funds and bonds as a result of market interest rate fluctuations.


Net gains on derecognition of financial assets measured at amortized cost amounted to RMB19,569 million, an increase of
RMB16,511 million, or 539.93% compared with the prior year. It was primarily due to the increase in the gains on the disposal
of debt instruments as the Bank continuously tracked market trends and made timely adjustments to its investment portfolio
structure; and an increase in the gains generated from the issuance of non-performing asset securitization products as the
Bank continuously intensified the disposal of non-performing assets.


Net other operating gains amounted to -RMB52 million, a decrease of RMB953 million compared with the prior year, primarily
due to the fluctuation of the exchange rate of the U.S. dollar against the RMB and the decrease in government subsidies.

Assets
The Bank thoroughly implemented the decisions and plans of the CPC Central Committee, and stayed true to the fundamental
purpose of serving the real economy with financial services. It aimed to advance the high-quality development of finance,
coordinated asset allocation in a sound way, and continued to offer more effective, balanced and sustainable services for the
real economy. During the reporting period, the Bank adhered to long-termism, kept a balance among scale, price and risks, and
deepened the application of RAROC in resource allocation, so as to further optimize its asset structure and enhance the value
creation capabilities. It consolidated the foundation for development, enhanced the building of core capabilities, and properly
integrated its own resource endowments with key areas of services to the real economy. It made solid and meticulous efforts
to promote the development of the “five priorities” of the financial sector, and allocated more financial resources to major
strategies, key areas, and weak links, striving to build a sound and balanced business structure. By strengthening the guidance
of investment research and keeping a close eye on market changes, the Bank optimized the non-credit business allocation
structure and enhanced the quality and efficiency of fund utilization.


As at the end of the reporting period, the Bank’s total assets amounted to RMB18,682,067 million, an increase of RMB1,597,157
million, or 9.35% from the prior year-end, of which net loans to customers amounted to RMB9,440,874 million, an increase of
RMB756,730 million, or 8.71% from the prior year-end; financial investments amounted to RMB6,358,153 million, an increase of
RMB354,026 million, or 5.90% from the prior year-end; loan-to-deposit ratio was 58.33%, an increase of 0.03 percentage point
from the prior year-end, indicating that the asset structure has been further optimized.

Financial Investments
During the reporting period, the Bank further implemented the transformation of its financial market business, adhered to the
guidance of investment research, actively seized opportunities arising from market fluctuations, optimized the asset allocation
structure, and maintained steady growth in the scale of financial investments. As at the end of the reporting period, the Bank’s
financial investments amounted to RMB6,358,153 million, an increase of RMB354,026 million, or 5.90% from the prior year-end.


In terms of products, the increase was primarily in the scale of debt securities, with the investment in debt securities reaching
RMB5,072,347 million, an increase of RMB434,384 million, or 9.37% from the prior year-end.


In terms of measurement approach, the increase was primarily driven by growth in the financial assets measured at amortized
cost and financial assets measured at fair value through other comprehensive income-debt instruments. Specifically, the
financial assets measured at amortized cost amounted to RMB4,688,443 million, an increase of RMB381,930 million, or 8.87%
from the prior year-end, mainly due to the increased investment in government bonds; and financial assets measured at fair
value through other comprehensive income-debt instruments amounted to RMB704,440 million, an increase of RMB35,628
million, or 5.33% from the prior year-end, primarily driven by the increase in investments in bonds issued by financial
institutions and interbank certificates of deposit.

Liabilities
The Bank earnestly implemented regulatory requirements, continuously improved the liability quality management framework,
and regarded high-quality liabilities as the basis for steady operations and the cornerstone for serving the real economy.
During the reporting period, the Bank continuously consolidated the scale and quality of customers and took general deposits
as the main component of core liability businesses, achieving steady growth in the scale of deposits and maintaining a
stable source of deposits. It adhered to the principle of balanced development between volume and price, strengthened
the refined pricing management, and promoted the steady decline of the cost of liabilities. It proactively diversified funding
channels, actively participated in market-oriented transactions, and enhanced the diversity of the liability structure. It made a
sound and coordinated arrangement for the total amount, structure and pace of fund taking and utilization, and achieved an
overall balance between liquidity and profitability. It adhered to compliance in business operations, carried out transactions,
accounting and statistics of liabilities in a legally compliant way, and firmly guarded against risks. The quality of the Bank’s
liability business improved steadily, with the relevant indicators performing well.


As at the end of the reporting period, the Bank’s total liabilities amounted to RMB17,519,722 million, an increase of
RMB1,466,461 million, or 9.13% from the prior year-end. Specifically, customer deposits amounted to RMB16,541,716 million,
an increase of RMB1,254,175 million, or 8.20% from the prior year-end; and deposits and placements from banks and other
financial institutions as well as financial assets sold under repurchase agreements amounted to a total of RMB500,806 million,
an increase of RMB123,384 million, or 32.69% from the prior year-end, mainly because the Bank optimized its liability structure
and seized opportunities to expand the scale of interbank liabilities.

Analysis of Cash Flow Statement
During the reporting period, net cash inflow generated from operating activities of the Bank was RMB412,059 million, an
increase of RMB14,783 million compared with the prior year, mainly due to the increase in cash received from businesses such
as debt securities sold under repurchase agreements compared with the prior year.


During the reporting period, net cash outflow used in investing activities of the Bank amounted to RMB175,934 million, a
decrease of RMB304,465 million compared with the prior year, primarily due to the decrease in cash paid for investment in
debt securities compared with the prior year.


During the reporting period, net cash inflow generated from financing activities of the Bank was RMB45,744 million, compared
with a net cash outflow of RMB30,778 million in the prior year, mainly due to the increase in cash received from the issuance
of A shares to specific subscribers.

     Deepening Institutional Reforms and Becoming Mass Affluent Customers’
     Primary Bank of Choice for Wealth Management Services                                                                                                                                           Column


     The Bank actively promoted the transformation of wealth management business, focused on process-based business
     model reform, enhanced five professional capabilities, including customer acquisition and activation, guidance of
     investment research, product selection, team building, and content operations, and strove to become the mass
     affluent customers’ primary bank of choice for wealth management services.
     The Bank strengthened customer acquisition and activation capabilities. It focused on the management of
     key customer segments, deepened asset allocation, and tapped into the growth potential of customer value. It
     also promoted the centralized operation model for private banking and enhanced its capabilities to serve high-
     net-worth customers. The Bank adhered to the guidance of investment research. It enhanced market analysis
     capabilities, established an investment research expert pool, built the wealth investment decision-making meeting
     mechanism, formulated allocation plans for major asset categories, captured market opportunities, and developed
     product selection plans. It also improved the daily, weekly, and monthly investment research report framework to
     deliver professional insights. The Bank developed superior product selection capabilities. It improved the product
     platform covering all categories and strategies to meet customers’ needs for diversified asset allocation. It also carefully
     selected advantageous products, built a key product pool, and won customers’ trust through professional competence.
     The Bank intensified team building. It solidified the talent foundation, established a tiered talent development
     mechanism, empowered wealth advisors through digital tools, and enhanced the professional capabilities of its
     workforce. The Bank improved its online operation capabilities. It iterated the wealth management channel on
     mobile banking and optimized online asset allocation experience through functions such as information delivery and
     wealth planning.
     The Bank reshaped its customer-centric, process-based work mechanism. It comprehensively developed a process-
     based operation model featuring the guidance of investment research, customer management, product selection, and team
     execution, ensured consistency between the Head Office and branches, met customers’ diverse needs for asset allocation,
     wealth inheritance, etc., and promoted the transformation and development of the wealth management business.
     Going forward, the Bank will continue to adhere to the customer-centric philosophy, deepen reform and innovation, improve
     professional capabilities to win customers’ trust, and promote the high-quality development of wealth management business.

Comprehensively Promoting Proactive Credit Extension to
                                                                                                                 Column
Create a Differentiated Growth Pole


Proactive credit extension to personal customers is an innovative online credit business model developed by the
Bank based on its strategic positioning and resource advantages, which is designed to achieve growth in credit
scale and comprehensive customer management at low operating costs. After three years of development since
the launch of proactive credit extension in September 2022, the program has achieved balanced and unified
development in four aspects, namely rapid business growth, effective risk control, low operating costs, and excellent
customer experience, becoming one of the Bank’s differentiated growth poles.


Regarding rapid business growth, as at the end of the reporting period, the balance of personal proactive credit
extension loans exceeded RMB350.0 billion, with a compound annual growth rate of 138% over the past three years.
Regarding effective risk control, the NPL ratio of loans granted through proactive credit extension was kept within
1%, significantly lower than that of similar businesses. Regarding low operating costs, customers of proactive credit
extension were mainly acquired through remote channels such as the mobile banking app, intelligent outbound
calls, and SMS in a targeted manner, and the full life-cycle management such as customer onboarding and loan
renewal was conducted by the headquarters via centralized and online operations, so the operating cost of proactive
credit extension was significantly lower than that of other businesses. Regarding excellent customer experience,
as the Bank proactively extended credit to customers, customers could quickly apply for loans through mobile
banking and enjoy an instant loan approval experience.


In addition, the Bank further enhanced its core capabilities through proactive credit extension, primarily in five
aspects, namely big data-driven list mining, multi-dimensional targeted marketing, minimalist product design,
intelligent risk management and control, and integrated post-lending management. Specifically, the Bank
leveraged big data technology to create customer profile tags from tens of thousands of dimensions and identified
high-quality customers and potential credit needs. It developed multi-dimensional targeted marketing capabilities
covering channels such as pop-ups, SMS, intelligent voice, and remote agents, introduced LLM tools to strengthen
human-machine collaboration, and improved marketing conversion efficiency. By deeply integrating back-office
data, the Bank simplified loan application procedures, enabled customers to obtain loans in as quick as three steps,
namely, authorization, authentication, and submission, and provided “One-Click Renewal” service. Focusing on big
data and AI, the Bank built an intelligent risk control framework encompassing the entire credit process, continuously
introduced various external data to improve the customer risk dashboard, developed real-time offensive and
defensive capabilities against telecommunications fraud and credit fraud, built an agile iteration mechanism for risk
control models and strategies, and ensured the effectiveness of risk control measures on an ongoing basis. The Bank
also strengthened post-lending AI early warnings, developed a full-chain integrated collection management model,
and efficiently resolved and handled risks. These core capabilities not only supported the development of proactive
credit extension but also empowered the development of retail credit business across the Bank.


Going forward, while firmly upholding the bottom line of risk control, the Bank will leverage new technologies such
as AI LLMs to enhance its core capabilities, strengthen the penetration and conversion of various customer segments,
improve the management of existing customers, and elevate proactive credit extension to a new level.

Building a Logistics Finance Ecosystem, Empowering Shipping Networks Through Finance Support
                                                                                                                     Column


The Bank fully implemented the CPC Central Committee’s major strategic plan of building a strong
maritime nation and a shipping power at a faster pace, focused on national strategic orientation and core
demands of industrial chains, and established an integrated financial service framework spanning the entire
“port-shipping-logistics-industry” chain through its special initiatives to boost logistics finance. Through various
measures including innovating service models based on local conditions, forming specialized service teams,
and designing tailored solutions, the Bank addressed financial needs in key scenarios such as port and shipping
infrastructure construction, industrial clustering, and logistics operations. This enabled precise allocation of financial
resources to critical nodes within the shipping ecosystem and demonstrated the Bank’s commitment as a major
state-owned bank to supporting the development of national shipping hub and modern port logistics system.


Closely following Tianjin’s strategic focus on “building a northern international shipping hub, concentrating shipping
resources, promoting high-quality integration of port, industry and urban development, and establishing a financial
innovation operation demonstration zone”, PSBC Tianjin Branch leveraged Tianjin’s port advantages as a pivot to
develop an all-encompassing maritime logistics finance service system and publicly released the Four-Domain
Support, Seven-Measure Promotion: Postal Savings Bank of China’s Shipping Financial Service Plan for Tianjin.
These efforts drove growth in the Bank’s shipping and logistics financing scale in Tianjin, facilitated breakthroughs
in its service model innovation, and enabled significant improvements in its service quality and efficiency. By fully
integrating into Tianjin’s development of international shipping hub, the Bank advanced deeper integration of port,
industry and urban development, and contributed sustained financial support to fostering a modern port industrial
cluster and building a world-class shipping and logistics hub.

Implementing Technology Finance Strategy to Foster Engines Driving New Quality Productive Forces
                                                                                                                Column


Following the guiding principles of the Central Financial Work Conference, the Bank focused on the development
requirements of technology finance, continuously improved its specialized and integrated financial service
framework, provided targeted support for technological innovation and industrial upgrading, and strove to address
the key links in the transformation of scientific and technological achievements, injecting financial momentum into
high-quality development and the cultivation of new quality productive forces.


Seizing the opportunities presented by the “sci-tech board” in the bond market, the Bank concentrated its
efforts on sci-tech innovation bonds. It underwrote the first batch of sci-tech innovation bonds in the market,
serving issuers including financial institutions, private enterprises, and equity investment institutions. On the one
hand, the Bank helped mature sci-tech enterprises expand their use of proceeds and financing channels, effectively
stimulating the technological innovation vitality of private enterprises. On the other hand, it provided equity
investment institutions with more convenient financing tools to make investment in the field of technological
innovation, guiding market capital to flow more precisely into “hard technology” sectors.


Actively implementing national strategies, the Bank issued its inaugural sci-tech innovation bonds. On August
19, 2025, it successfully completed the book building and issuance of RMB5 billion of sci-tech innovation bonds in
the National Interbank Bond Market. The issuance consisted of both fixed-rate and floating-rate tranches, both of
which received wide recognition and strong investor subscription. This issuance marked the Bank’s inaugural sci-tech
innovation bond. Notably, Tranche II represented both the market’s first three-year floating-rate sci-tech innovation
bond and the first floating-rate sci-tech innovation bond issued via the ChinaBond blockchain-enabled book building
and issuance system. The proceeds will be primarily directed toward technology R&D and industrialization projects
that are aligned with national strategies, thereby continuously contributing to China’s strength in science and
technology.


The Bank proactively developed M&A loans for technology enterprises, supporting their integration
efforts and advancing the development of new quality productive forces. Guided by the philosophy of
innovation-driven development, the Bank focused on the core objective of strengthening and supplementing
industrial chains for technology enterprises, leveraged M&A finance as a tool to empower resource integration and
value enhancement of technology enterprises, and built a comprehensive financial service framework covering
the entire lifecycle of technology enterprises. During the reporting period, the Bank successfully extended nearly
RMB3.7 billion in M&A loans to technology enterprises, effectively supporting a number of high-quality technology
enterprises in their M&A activities and providing important financial support for the development of new quality
productive forces.

Launching the First Proactive Credit Extension and Discounting Product to Inject
                                                                                                                                               Column
New Financial Vitality into MSEs


To continuously support the development of MSEs, the Bank launched “Inclusive Discount”, a dedicated discounting
product for MSEs. By introducing a proactive credit extension mechanism, the Bank provided one-stop, self-service
exclusive bill financing services for MSEs tailored to their financing characteristics, namely small transaction
amounts and high transaction frequency. In October 2025, the Bank successfully held the “Bill Connects Hundreds
of Businesses, PSBC Benefits Thousands of Industries” Summit and “Inclusive Discount” product launch event in Linyi
City, Shandong Province. The product won widespread acclaim from participating enterprises. As at the end of the
reporting period, the Bank successfully approved low-risk limits for over 9,000 MSEs through “Inclusive Discount”.


“Inclusive Discount” boasts three core advantages. First, it features efficiency and convenience. Through an online,
intelligent risk control LLM, it has reduced the review time of discounting limit application for MSEs from T+2 to
T+0. Second, it features diversification and integration. By integrating with online discounting products such as
“Smart Instant Discount”, “PSBC E Discounting”, and “Sci-Tech Discounting”, it can quickly match different products
to different discounting needs of MSEs across various industries and with varying financing preferences, thereby
delivering personalized and tailored services. Third, it features proactive services. It automatically identifies potential
customer needs and matches them with financial services, injecting strong momentum into enterprise development.


Going forward, the Bank will further optimize and iterate the algorithm model of “Inclusive Discount”, continuously

     Innovating the Interbank Financing Model and Creating a New
                                                                                                                            Column
     Interbank Finance Ecosystem


     The Bank has launched a pledged interbank deposit product for banking clients. The product uses high-grade bonds
     as collateral and leverages the specialized collateral management system of the China Central Depository & Clearing
     Co., Ltd. (CCDC) for fully automated end-to-end management, providing counterparties with funding services with a
     term of less than one year. As at the end of the reporting period, the scale of the Bank’s pledged interbank deposits
     amounted to nearly RMB200 billion, becoming an important vehicle for the Bank to deepen interbank cooperation
     and achieve mutually beneficial and win-win cooperation. The product won the “Market Innovation Award” in the
     interbank local currency market and the “Social Responsibility Institution Award for Collateral Business” from the
     CCDC. It was also widely reported by mainstream media outlets such as Securities Daily.


     Leveraging an online and standardized innovative operational model, the pledged interbank deposit offers an
     “efficient and low-cost” short-to-medium-term funding solution for interbank clients. The product has four major
     features. First, it helps clients effectively revitalize existing assets. Instead of transferring bond ownership, clients only
     need to pledge eligible bonds for obtaining financial support from the Bank at a lower cost. Second, supplemented
     by low-risk credit lines, it helps clients obtain additional stable and sufficient financing. Third, it precisely meets
     clients’ needs in terms of financing terms, covering all liquidity needs within one year. Fourth, the business process is
     efficient and convenient, and fully online and automated, with the entire process, from application to disbursement,
     completed as quickly as on the same day, timely meeting clients’ liquidity needs.


     Going forward, the Bank will continuously enhance the quality and promote the development of pledged
     interbank deposits, provide service solutions featuring more ample limits, more precise pricing, and more efficient
     delivery to accurately meet the financing needs of clients in the interbank ecosystem, further deepen cooperation
     with interbank clients, and jointly build a new interbank finance ecosystem characterized by openness, sharing,
     complementary advantages, and win-win cooperation.

     Leading Industry Investment Research Innovation and Building a New
                                                                                                                                                                              Column
     Engine for Digital and Intelligent Investment Research

     To promote the digital transformation of financial market business and strengthen investment research support, the Bank officially
     launched the investment research and decision-making system, marking a solid step forward in “smart investment research”. The system
     made extensive use of big data analysis and AI technologies, covered key areas such as market research, investment decision-making,
     strategy management and risk analysis, achieved digital and intelligent coverage of the entire research lifecycle, and injected new vitality
     into high-quality development.

     Building a new smart investment research system covering six core scenarios
     The investment research and decision-making system covers six core application scenarios. Specifically, the “Market Observation”
     provides panoramic analysis of five major topics, namely market dynamics, funds, policies, fundamentals, and institutional behaviors;
     the “Index Analysis” supports strategy simulation and time-series research; the “Credit Bond Research” leverages to a great extent the
     internal and external data of issuers and bonds, intelligently generates a panoramic risk profile, and supports dynamic trial pricing
     calculations and real-time market anomaly warnings for credit bonds; the “Risk Research” develops a three-dimensional risk monitoring
     system encompassing credit, market, and liquidity and conducts full-process transaction analysis based on dimensions such as accounts,
     products, traders, and counterparties; the “Strategy Management” supports the creation of strategy trees and execution tracking; and the
     “Research Library” pools internal and external research results and supports intelligent preparation of investment research reports.

     Deepening intelligent application and achieving capability enhancement across entire process
     Firstly, the system aggregates multi-dimensional investment research data to create a unified data foundation. The system integrates
     multi-dimensional data resources such as macroeconomic indicators, issuer credit ratings, asset market trends, and transaction data,
     providing comprehensive support for investment research and analysis. Secondly, it develops an integrated investment research platform
     to achieve full-cycle closed-loop management. The system supports full-process management encompassing market research, strategy
     deduction, execution tracking, and result output, helping to achieve the goal of “investment research and strategy-driven approach”.
     Thirdly, it innovates intelligent interaction experience to improve research and decision-making efficiency. Based on LLM technology, the
     system has developed an “AI assistant for investment research” that supports intelligent Q&As regarding issuers, bonds, and knowledge
     bases and assists researchers in quickly gaining insights into market dynamics and risk changes.

     The investment research and decision-making system has set a new paradigm for data management and application in the financial
     sector. It is highly recognized within the industry and was selected as one of the “Top 100 Data Management Excellent Cases in 2025” by
     the China Federation of Electronics and Information Industry. In the future, the Bank will focus on the three areas of intelligent assistance,
     precise decision-making, and efficient collaboration, continuously optimize system functions, advance AI-powered application, build
     a new digital and intelligent investment research ecosystem, and provide solid technological support for serving national strategies,
     empowering the real economy, and enhancing the service capabilities of the financial market.

     Fulfilling the Responsibility and Mission of a Major Bank and Setting a New
     Benchmark for Financial Services in Summer Grain Purchase

     Summer harvest, planting, and management are crucial for a bumper harvest and agricultural stability throughout the
     year. In 2025, the Bank established a special working group for summer grain purchase, and implemented a special
     service initiative for summer grain purchase. It formulated a package of special policies targeting core production areas,
     and provided grain purchase brokers and other customers with policies such as higher credit limits during peak seasons
     and preferential interest rates, achieving an overall improvement in business scale, efficiency, and customer experience
     and contributing financial power to ensuring China’s food supply. During the reporting period, the Bank issued over
     RMB36.0 billion of micro loans for summer grain purchase, a year-on-year increase of more than 28%; and the net increase
     was over RMB14.0 billion, a year-on-year increase of more than 27%.


                        Henan
              PSBC Henan Branch acted on the guiding principles of early deployment, early publicity, and early
              credit extension, encouraged customer managers to provide on-site services, and precisely met the
              financial needs of grain purchase clients. In early April 2025, the branch launched its summer grain
              purchase service initiative, conducted market research, and formulated special service plans. Leaders at
              all levels of branches and sub-branches actively acted as chief service officers, engaged with platforms
              such as agricultural credit guarantee companies, food administrations, bureaus of agriculture and
              rural affairs, and Sinograin reserve warehouses, and understood and grasped the market information
              about summer grain purchase. Branches and sub-branches in cities and counties acted
              swiftly and provided targeted services, conducted grid-based visits in a tiered and

Building a Scenario-Based Financial Ecosystem to Empower the Digital
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Column
Transformation of SMEs


In the wave of the digital economy, the digital transformation of SMEs has shifted from an option for development to a prerequisite for survival.
The Bank remained true to the original aspiration of developing inclusive finance, deeply integrated financial technology resources with
practical experience in serving the real economy, and continuously upgraded the “Easy Corporate Operation” one-stop digital management
platform for enterprises to enhance its service capabilities and empower the transformation and upgrading of enterprises across the entire
business chain. As at the end of the reporting period, the Bank had provided efficient, intelligent, and secure digital solutions for over 170
thousand SMEs in over 20 industries in total.

With a focus on growth-oriented SMEs, the “Easy Corporate Operation” platform provided customized solutions tailored to the specific
operating characteristics of each industry. For wholesale and retail enterprises, the platform addressed pain points such as complex upstream
procurement management, numerous downstream orders, and inefficient business-finance reconciliation. For processing and manufacturing
enterprises, it provided comprehensive services including production process management, piece-rate wage calculation, business and finance
integrated collaboration, and standardized management of procurement. For service enterprises, it focused on addressing practical challenges
such as high volume of payment distribution, large invoicing requests, and difficulties in invoice management. For construction engineering
enterprises, it created an integrated solution encompassing financial management, workforce coordination, decentralized attendance
management, diversified payroll calculation, and independent tax declaration for multiple projects. For agricultural enterprises, it adapted to
industry-specific accounting standards and offered services such as reverse invoicing and purchase, sales and inventory management, helping
enterprises achieve a digital upgrade in finance and taxation processing. Through comprehensive innovation of traditional management
models, the platform helped enterprises effectively reduce operating costs and improve decision-making efficiency.

In 2025, the Bank further enriched the scenario-based ecosystem of the “Easy Corporate Operation” platform to reach a wider range of inclusive
finance customers. The Bank iteratively upgraded the platform to version 3.0, added two application scenarios, namely supplier bidding (Easy
Bidding) and Easy Industrial Park, established an ecosystem-based partnership with Meituan, launched vertical industry services such as HRO
(Human Resources Outsourcing) and piece-rate wages, and introduced a dedicated version for technology enterprises, continuously creating
high-value service solutions for enterprises. Meanwhile, the Bank strengthened customer service support on the “Easy Corporate Operation”
platform. On the one hand, focusing on industries where SMEs are relatively concentrated, the Bank adhered to a “one industry per quarter”
strategy and delivered tailored industry solutions by quarter. On the other hand, the Bank launched a new year interface, produced function
demonstration videos, updated operation manuals, provided system page operation guides, and distributed customer surveys on the platform
to optimize customer experience in all aspects.

Going forward, the Bank will adhere to the customer-centric philosophy, leverage its open banking architecture and advanced IT capabilities,
drive the function upgrading and ecosystem expansion of the “Easy Corporate Operation” platform, further advance the “scenario plus
finance” integrated model, and further expand service boundaries and improve service precision, to enable more SMEs to benefit from digital
transformation, inject continuous financial momentum into the high-quality development of the real economy, and work hand in hand with
SMEs on a new journey of digital transformation.

104   Postal Savings Bank of China Co., Ltd. | 2025 Annual Report
                                                                      Discussion and         Corporate       Financial Statements
                                                   Overview              Analysis           Governance           and Others
                                                                     Business Overview




In response to the national call and to support the strategy of boosting China’s strength in science and technology, the Board
of Directors of the Bank considered and approved the proposal to establish a financial asset investment subsidiary on July 16,
2025. The Bank intended to invest RMB10 billion with its own funds to initiate the establishment of a financial asset investment
company as the investment entity in accordance with the Management Measures for Financial Asset Investment Companies
(Trial). On October 21, 2025, the NFRA approved the Bank’s plan to establish the PSBC Investment. During the preparatory
phase, all preparatory work for PSBC Investment, including corporate governance, business planning, risk management, system
support, and institutional framework construction, was steadily advanced on all fronts. On March 16, 2026, the NFRA approved
the commencement of operations of PSBC Financial Asset Investment Co., Ltd. On March 20, PSBC Investment was officially
established.


PSBC Investment has a registered capital of RMB10 billion, in which the Bank holds a 100% stake. Its business scope is: acquiring
banks’ claims on enterprises for the purpose of debt-to-equity swaps, converting such claims into equity, and managing the
resulting equity interests; restructuring, transferring, or disposing of claims that cannot be converted into equity; investing
in enterprise equity for the purpose of debt-to-equity swaps, with the invested funds to be used by enterprises solely for
repaying existing claims; raising funds from qualified investors and issuing private asset management products in accordance
with laws and regulations to support debt-to-equity swap implementation; issuing financial bonds; raising funds through bond
repurchases, interbank lending, and interbank borrowing; conducting necessary investment management of proprietary funds
and raised funds, where proprietary funds may be used for deposits and placements with banks, and purchases of government
bonds or other fixed-income securities, and raised funds shall be used in accordance with the intended purposes specified in
the fundraising agreements; providing financial advisory and consulting services related to debt-to-equity swap business; and
other businesses approved by the NFRA.


PSBC Investment is a key component of the Bank’s comprehensive service strategy. As an important platform for the Bank to
implement the “five priorities” of the financial sector, the company will focus on the primary responsibility and core businesses
of serving the real economy. It will leverage the Bank’s extensive network, customer base and strong brand, focus on
debt-to-equity swaps as its main business, and take as its mission channeling more resources toward “early-stage, small-scale,
long-term and hard-tech” projects. Through an integrated “financing plus advisory” service model, it aims to optimize and
upgrade traditional industries, foster the growth of emerging and future industries, and establish itself as a “national team” and
the “main force” in equity investment. PSBC Investment will build a loan-investment linkage innovation platform, a long-term
capital platform for technological innovation, a debt-to-equity swap platform for structural reform, and an equity investment
management platform to uphold the Bank’s strategic positioning and build the Bank into an emerging force in technology
finance.




During the reporting period, the Bank’s absorption and merger of YOU+ BANK was approved by the NFRA. As of December
29, 2025 (the regulatory approval date), YOU+ BANK had total assets of RMB10,974 million and total liabilities of RMB6,998
million, and was merged into the Bank on the same day. As a wholly-owned subsidiary of the Bank, its financial statements
were consolidated into the Bank’s financial statements at a 100% proportion. This absorption and merger aligns with the
Bank’s long-term strategic plan, will not affect the Bank’s financial position or operating results, nor will it harm the interests
of the Bank or its shareholders. As at the Latest Practicable Date, YOU+ BANK has completed the industrial and commercial
deregistration.

      Building New “AI plus Finance” Infrastructure and Creating a
      New Paradigm for Financial Services                                                                                                                                                                   Column


      The Bank has built an AI architecture framework encompassing computing power, algorithms, data, security, and scenarios, and achieved
      centralized deployment, unified access, and visualized management of LLMs. This supports business departments in rapidly building agent
      applications with “zero code”, significantly lowering the threshold for AI adoption, accelerating technology implementation at PSBC speed, and
      the full embracing of the new era of “AI plus finance”.

      The Bank’s LLM development covers more than 260 application scenarios across the front, middle, and back-office. It has opened up 24 general
      AI capabilities of 10 major categories to all branches, and formed PSBC’s “AI2ALL” digital ecosystem featuring “external omnichannel reach plus
      internal Bank-wide efficiency enhancement”.

      In improving the quality of customer services, the Bank built an intelligent outbound calling system to deliver human-like intelligent outbound
      calls with end-to-end second-level response. It developed intelligent recommendation models covering all retail customer segments, all product
      categories and all channels, and achieved over RMB6 billion in personal credit extension and more than RMB1.4 billion in wealth product sales.
      The Bank enabled intelligent inquiry and response for bond underwriting transactions with the bond trading bot “You Xiaobao”, and improved
      the efficiency of transaction execution by over 95%. The Bank also fully connected the bill trading bot “You Xiaoying” to the “Together We
      Thrive” interbank ecosystem platform, improving the execution efficiency by approximately 10 times, with the cumulative transaction volume
      exceeding RMB1 trillion. Digital employees were fully deployed in core online and offline channels such as mobile banking and intelligent teller
      machines (ITMs). Online, they handled cumulatively nearly 50 million dialogues, and served over ten million users. Offline, they supported nearly
      100 high-frequency ITM business scenarios and improved the operational efficiency by about 40%.

      In enhancing the efficiency of internal operations and management, the Bank developed an intelligent review hub based on image-text
      understanding and multimodal information processing capabilities, empowering more than 20 business scenarios, with an image classification
      recognition rate reaching approximately 98%, and a key information extraction accuracy rate standing at about 92%. In the field of intelligent
      operations, the Bank overcame challenges in intelligent recognition and review of more than 40 types of bills and vouchers, with a classification
      accuracy rate exceeding 95%. The intelligent data assistant tool of the Bank provided data services featuring “queries in plain language,
      accurate answers, visual presentation, and on-demand availability” for over 20 thousand management personnel and business backbones at
      the Head Office and branches, with a result adoption rate exceeding 95%. The intelligent tracing tool helped the Bank realize field-level data
      lineage mapping, which covered more than 5 million fields, and helped R&D personnel resolve pain points such as data issue location and
      impact analysis. The Bank launched a total of 17 agents, including intelligent meeting, intelligent review and approval, and document drafting.
      They supported meeting reservation and automatic generation of meeting minutes, and handled over 220 thousand queries with intelligent
      knowledge answers, effectively reducing labor costs and enhancing employees’ intelligent working capabilities.

      Looking ahead, the Bank will remain committed to its original aspiration of serving the people through financial services, deepen the
      development of the “AI2ALL” digital ecosystem, and transform technological power into perceptive and warm financial services that reach
      thousands of industries and benefit millions of households. PSBC is dedicated to co-creating and sharing a better digital future with customers,
      partners, and society.

      Comprehensively Enhancing Data Capabilities and
      Driving Business Innovation with Data Elements                                                                                   Column


      During the 14th Five-Year Plan period, the Bank took data as a core strategic asset and systematically advanced the adoption of the
      mechanism “using assessments to drive development, governance, and application”, and comprehensively strengthened the development
      of data management framework. In terms of strategy, the Bank completed its 14th Five-Year Plan data planning and proactively arranged
      its data management and empowerment path during the 15th Five-Year Plan period. In terms of governance, it established a Data and
      Model Governance Committee and achieved integrated, full-lifecycle governance of data and models. In terms of mechanism, governance
      requirements were integrated into the key stages of R&D and application, achieving sustained rigorous control over 234 systems. In terms
      of technology, the Bank strengthened the self-development of big data and AI technologies to promote the intelligent upgrading of
      management paradigms. In addition, the Bank proactively shared its best practices in data governance and actively participated in the
      formulation of national and industry standards, fully demonstrating the exemplary and leading role of a large state-owned bank.

      The Bank has published the PSBC Data Asset White Paper for
      four consecutive years, continuously exploring and establishing
      mechanisms to unlock the value of data assets. During the
      reporting period, the Bank focused on realizing the multiplier
      effect of data elements and continued to advance data asset
      management. The 2025 edition of the White Paper, themed on
      “all-domain, efficiency, and sharing”, emphasized the dual drivers
      of management and operation. It brought together data insights
      from both the Head Office and branches across three dimensions,
      i.e. data asset management framework, management practices,
      and application practices, and released 34 data asset practice cases
      in areas such as customer services and risk prevention and control,
      laying a solid foundation for data-driven business development.

      During the reporting period, the Bank continued to improve its multidimensional retail customer profiling system and established an
      intelligent marketing model system covering multiple channels and supporting refined identification. By embedding capabilities of data
      analysis models into customer-reaching channels such as CRM, mobile banking, and intelligent outbound calling, the Bank upgraded its
      customer operation model from passive response to proactive service. The Bank also actively utilized deep learning and other algorithms
      to refine online channel operation. By developing models to unlock customer potential and reactivate dormant customers, it supported
      the Head Office and branches at all levels in conducting precision marketing through IT systems such as CRM and the marketing middle-
      office platform. This drove the transformation of its operating model from “manually seeking out customers” to “identifying customers via
      IT systems”, enabling precise customer identification and outreach across their different lifecycle stages, and effectively supporting the
      steady growth of active mobile banking users. In addition, the Bank actively applied advanced technologies including graph computing,
      empowered supply chain finance services with intelligent means, derived insights into financial service needs from complex industrial
      relationship data, and optimized product recommendation strategies, making financial services much more precise and forward-looking.

Ushering in the i∞PSBC Era and Building a New Multi-Dimensional
Intelligent Ecosystem                                                                                                               Column


The Bank thoroughly implemented the guiding principles of the Central Financial Work Conference, continuously advanced the key
tasks of “Digital Finance”, and held the Digital Finance Conference for three consecutive years to release its achievements of digital
financial services in a concentrated manner.

Against the backdrop of digital technology profoundly reshaping the financial landscape, the Bank advanced the development of
the Digital PSBC step by step following the principles of “Grasping the Trend, Reshaping the Foundation, Being Human-Centered,
and Pursuing Collaboration”. “Grasping the Trend” refers to conforming to the trend of digital economy and AI development, and
transforming technological changes into the internal driving force for high-quality development. “Reshaping the Foundation”
means to strengthen the digital infrastructure and core capability base, and consolidate the development foundation for
independent control and stable operation. “Being Human-Centered” refers to adhering to the customer-centered approach, and
making digital financial services reach every household. “Pursuing Collaboration” refers to achieving the integration of digital
technology and financial services through internal and external collaboration and ecological co-construction.

The Bank is committed to building the “AI2ALL” digital ecosystem and promoting the upgrade of intelligent technologies from
single-point applications to systematic empowerment.

In terms of capability, the Bank continuously strengthened the development of basic capabilities such as data, computing power
and algorithms, and promoted the transformation of AI from technical support to a business engine. Centering on customer scale,
experience depth, scenario coverage and detail innovation, the Bank planned over 260 AI application scenarios, and gradually
established an application system covering operation and management as well as customer service. It has received the first prize of
the FinTech Development Award of the PBOC for three consecutive years.

In terms of efficiency, the Bank empowered organizational operations with intelligent tools. The front office enhanced its targeted
marketing and customer reach capabilities through intelligent profiling and strategy models. The middle office drove the
mutually reinforcing improvement between risk control and business efficiency through intelligent models. The back office used
intelligent data assistant and other intelligent analysis tools to lower the threshold for data usage, and enhance the efficiency of
decision-making of the management and professional support for employees.

In terms of services, the Bank promoted the application of AI to offline, remote and online service scenarios, and built a
multi-touchpoint collaborative service system. Offline outlets crossed the boundaries of physical services through human-machine
collaboration. Relying on intelligent outbound calling, the Bank achieved efficient and proactive response to customer demand
with its remote services. As for its online services, the Bank took mobile banking as the core platform to continuously advance
intelligent interaction, scenario linkage and security protection, promoting an overall improvement in customer experience.

In addition, the Bank, with the launch of the mobile banking 11.0, continuously upgraded its service model in line with the
overall goal of “smart companionship, scenario interconnection, and trustworthy service”. In terms of interactive experience, AI
technologies have been further integrated into the customer journey, and a conversation-based service model was introduced to
explore high-frequency business processing through natural language. In terms of scenario-based services, through personalized
and intelligent display of homepage and to-do list, the Bank gradually transformed its services from “people searching for
functions” to “functions understanding people”. In terms of security guarantees, the Bank innovatively introduced a “relatives
and friends plus banks” dual protection mechanism to enhance the risk identification and collaborative protection capabilities,
continuously consolidating the foundation of user trust. In the latest 2025 China Digital Banking Survey Report released by CFCA,
the Bank's mobile banking ranked first in user experience for three consecutive years.

Strengthening the Talent Development Foundation and Building a Full-Cycle Growth System for New Recruits


The Bank has launched the “U+ Talent” series of new graduates employment and development programs since
2021. It rolled out programs such as “U+ Training Camp” and “U+ Practice Camp” to offer campus recruits platforms
for onboarding training and grassroots-level practice, with a mentoring system running through the entire talent
cultivation journey. The development cycle covered both the onboarding and career growth stages. To promote
standardized new recruits training and provide more well-conceived and effective onboarding training, the Bank
innovatively introduced a model featuring “mandatory plus elective” modules, and adopted a systematic approach to
new recruits training across the Bank.

In 2025, the Bank continued to advance the Head Office’s “U Series” talent cultivation programs, carried forward the
theme “U Shine at PSBC”, and promoted coordinated efforts between the Head Office and branches. The Head Office
delivered standardized mandatory modules, while branches customized content to cover corporate culture, job skills,
and professional competence. During the reporting period, approximately 5,200 new recruits participated in the
programs with positive results. These programs supported their smooth transition from “students” to “professionals”,
accelerated their growth from “shining individually” to “shining together”, and continuously injected youthful
vitality into the Bank’s high-quality development. During the same period, the Head Office launched the 2025 “U+
Mentor” training and certification program, built a pool of more than 500 mentors from all departments of the Head
Office, and formed a virtuous cycle of mentoring, guidance and expertise transfer. The Bank also organized the “U+
Practice Camp” for graduate recruits, assigned 199 graduate recruits to engage in grassroots-level practice in 14
cities of eight provinces, continuously optimized the practice training model, developed a grassroots-level practice
assessment system, and strengthened full-cycle management. In addition, the Bank improved the Head Office-
branch collaborative cultivation mechanism, built a talent cultivation system providing targeted empowerment and
facilitating efficient collaboration, constantly strengthened the workforce development, and empowered employee
growth.

Human Resources and Institution Management

The Bank adhered to the principle of “paying for job value, paying for work performance, and paying for
individual capabilities” and continuously improved the employee remuneration allocation mechanism. The
Bank implemented the requirements of the central government and higher-level authorities on remuneration
allocation management, strengthened remuneration allocation management, and regulated the order of internal
allocation. It continued to tilt remuneration distribution toward talents who made outstanding contributions and
frontline staff, improving the effectiveness of the incentive and constraint mechanism. The Bank implemented
full-staff performance management, strengthened the application of performance appraisal results, and gave full
play to the guiding role of performance appraisal. The Bank’s employee remuneration consisted of basic salary,
performance-based remuneration, and statutory welfare income such as social insurance and housing provident
fund. The basic salary reflected job value and personal competence, while the performance-based remuneration
focused on work achievements and performance. The Bank’s senior management and employees in positions with
a significant impact on risk were subject to a deferred payment and clawback mechanism for performance-based
remuneration, which guided employees to effectively balance business development and risk prevention, so as to
promote the healthy and sustainable development of the Bank. The Bank also kept optimizing its benefits system
to raise welfare benefits and enhance employees’ sense of belonging.


Employees
As at the end of the reporting period, the Bank had a total of 196,779 employees, among which, 182,347 were
contract employees (including 1,249 in majority-owned subsidiaries) and 14,432 were from labor dispatch
agencies. The number of retired employees of the Bank was 35,048. During the reporting period, the Bank
reasonably controlled headcount size while steadily improving talent quality. The percentage of employees
with a bachelor’s degree or above in the Bank continued to increase, and the distribution of employees across
positions has been further improved, with more human resources flowing to core business areas and front-office
marketing positions in an orderly manner. The Bank values gender diversity among employees. As at the end of
the reporting period, the percentages of male employees and female employees (including senior management
members) of the Bank were approximately 40.68% and 59.32%, respectively. The Bank has maintained a diverse
workforce with a balanced gender distribution.

Human Resources and Institution Management

Institution Management
The Head Office of the Bank is located in Beijing and serves as the decision-making and management center of the Bank. The
Bank’s tier-1 branches are situated in the provincial capitals, capitals of autonomous regions, municipalities directly under
the Central Government, and separate-planning cities. As the operation and management center within the corresponding
regions, tier-1 branches are responsible for managing all institutions in their respective areas and reporting directly to the Head
Office. Tier-2 branches are generally set up in the prefecture-level cities in provinces and autonomous regions. In addition to
their operation and management functions, tier-2 branches are also responsible for managing subordinate institutions and
reporting to their supervisory tier-1 branches. Tier-1 sub-branches primarily undertake the functions of business operations
and outlet management, and report to their supervisory tier-2 branches. Tier-2 sub-branches primarily undertake the function
of business operations.


During the reporting period, the Bank continued to optimize its organizational structure to better support the implementation
of its strategies and business development. Regarding internal institutions, the Bank advanced the development of the
“five priorities” of the financial sector, and adjusted and established the Personal Banking Department (the Pension Finance
Department and Consumer Protection Center) and the Inclusive Finance Department (the Technology Finance Center);
established the Wealth Management Department to support the development of wealth management business; implemented
the relevant requirements of the reform of the Board of Supervisors and dissolved the Office of the Board of Supervisors of the
Head Office.


As at the end of the reporting period, the Bank had 7,758 institutions, including the Head Office, 36 tier-1 branches, 326 tier-2
branches, 2,220 tier-1 sub-branches, 5,172 tier-2 sub-branches, as well as majority-owned subsidiaries, including PSBC Wealth
Management and PSBC Consumer Finance. For details, please refer to “Business Overview – Majority-owned Subsidiaries” of
this report.

Interest Rate Risk in Banking Book

Management of Interest Rate Risk in Banking Book
Interest rate risk in banking book refers to the risk that causes losses to the economic value and overall earnings of the banking
book due to adverse changes in interest rates and maturity structure, etc. The interest rate risk in the Bank’s banking book
mainly arises from the mismatch between the repricing periods of assets and liabilities as well as the inconsistent changes in
their pricing basis. During the reporting period, the overall interest rate risk in the Bank’s banking book remained stable, and
key risk indicators remained within the established limits.


For interest rate risk in the banking book, the Bank has established a management framework and a governance structure
tailored to its characteristics. Based on factors such as the macroeconomic environment, market dynamics and risk appetite,
the Bank implements a prudent interest rate risk management strategy for the banking book, which mainly includes methods
such as repricing gap analysis, sensitivity analysis of net interest income and economic value, limit management, duration
management, scenario simulation, and proactive adjustments to the asset-liability structure. The Bank closely monitored
domestic and international economic and financial conditions, actively carried out forward-looking management, continuously
optimized the duration structure of assets and liabilities, continuously promoted staggered loan repricing, comprehensively
conducted multiple scenario simulations such as stress testing, maintained a balance among volume, pricing, and risk as well
as a balance between current earnings and long-term value.
